message.content: The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its energy demands. In most eukaryotic cells you’ll find anywhere from a few dozen to several thousand mitochondria—often ranging between 50 and 10,000 per cell. Cells with high metabolic activity, such as muscle or liver cells, tend to have the upper end of that range, while less active cells may contain fewer.
